title: Measurement of the pupillary light reflex after critical illness
summary: With this study we strive to find out, if patients who had been treated on an intensive care unit and who suffer from intensive-care-unit-aquired weakness (ICU-AW) show additional alterations of the pupillary light reflex when compared to age-matched controls.

interventions.name:
Patients who developed an intensive care unit aquired weakness after critical illness and who do not require analgosedation. Timepoint of measurement normally would be briefly prior to discharge to an rehabilitation unit. There is a single time-point for the following measurements:

Age-matched control persons without critical illness.
There is a single time-point for the following measurements:
- Maximum and minimum pupil diameter
- Latency of constriction
- Constriction velocity
- Maximum constriction velocity
- Dilation velocity

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Signed informed consent (by participant or legal guardian)
Exclusion criteria:
- acute or chronic severe neurological disease (progressive dementia, degenerative disease of the central nervous system)
- Diseases of the optic system (e.g. glaucoma, macula degeneration, macula degeneration, cerebral infarction of parts of the optic tracts and radiation)
- Current treatment with centrally acting medication with effects on the pupillary light reaction (e.g. opioids and porpofol)
Current treatment with medication directly modifying the pupillary light reaction (medication with mydriatic effects, medication with miotic effects (e.g. parasympathmimetic medication)
